hook.text: A steel coupon weighed before and after a year in seawater tells you exactly how fast it's dissolving.

buildup.text: Weight loss coupons are the simplest method — divide mass lost by area and time to get corrosion rate.

discovery.text: Electrochemical methods like linear polarization give real-time corrosion rates without waiting months.

twist.text: Uniform corrosion is predictable — but localized pitting can perforate a pipe while average thickness looks fine.

climax.text: Oil and gas pipelines run corrosion monitoring systems 24/7 — catching attacks before they cause leaks.

punchline.text: You can't fight corrosion if you can't measure it.

quiz.question: Why can average corrosion rate be misleading?
options: Localized pitting can penetrate before average thickness drops noticeably
It only works on stainless steel
